Working notes for east-region large request routing.

- Do not rely on option letters alone. Labels vary/truncate, especially C. Verify full option text before choosing.
- Refunds: route to regional office only when the message says it came through the regional office. REQ-2401 accepted; REQ-2406 rejected for regional office without that cue.
- Claims: regional office accepted for routine claims such as “Let me know if anything is missing” and “paperwork scanned” (REQ-2407, REQ-2409). Claim described as “same as the ones I sent last month” was accepted via priority desk (B) (REQ-2404).
- Invoices: regional office generally invalid/rejected (REQ-2400, REQ-2402, REQ-2408). Exception: REQ-2403, invoice from Finance Desk, option C was accepted, but its full label was unclear/truncated. If an invoice originates from Finance Desk, prefer Finance Desk routing if offered; otherwise do not route invoices to regional office.
- Invalid choices: C regional office for invoices; D as an option; C regional office for refunds without a regional-office cue.
- Sender department may matter, but message cues are stronger. Use request type + cue first.
- Next decisions: inspect full option labels; for claims, use regional office unless “same as last month” cue suggests priority desk; for refunds, require regional-office cue; for invoices, avoid regional office unless a Finance Desk route is available.

Working notes for east-region large request routing.

- Verify full option text; labels vary/truncate, especially C. Do not choose by letter alone.
- Invoices: A standard queue is invalid (REQ-2410, 2411, 2415, 2416, 2419). B priority desk can be valid when the client has repeatedly chased (“asking about this twice already”, REQ-2412). C regional office generally invalid for invoices (REQ-2400, 2402, 2408); only possible exception was REQ-2403, an invoice from Finance Desk where C was accepted but label was unclear. If a clear Finance Desk route is offered, prefer it; otherwise avoid A and regional office for invoices.
- Claims: C regional office accepted for routine claims (“Let me know if anything is missing”; “paperwork scanned”), including from Finance Desk (REQ-2407, 2409, 2413). Exception: “same as the ones I sent last month” went to B priority desk (REQ-2404).
- Refunds: correct old rule. C regional office is not justified by “came in through regional office” alone: REQ-2414 rejected C from Finance Desk despite that cue. A standard queue accepted a Regional Ops refund with “No rush…” (REQ-2418). C accepted earlier (REQ-2401) but conditions unclear. For refunds, check sender and full label; do not default to C.
- Shipments: B priority desk rejected for “Hoping this can go out before end of day” (REQ-2417); urgency wording alone does not imply B.
- Invalid/risky: A for invoices; B for shipment urgency; C for invoices generally; C for refunds unless clearly supported; D generally.
- Order: request type first, then sender department and message cue; verify labels before deciding.

Working notes for east-region large request routing.

- Always read full option text; labels vary/truncate, especially C. Do not choose by letter alone.
- Order: request type first, then sender department and message cue; verify labels before deciding.
- Invoices: A invalid. C regional office generally invalid (2400, 2402, 2408; 2403 unclear Finance Desk exception). B can be valid for invoices when client repeatedly chased (“asking twice”, 2412, 2427) or “same as the ones I sent last month” (2429). B rejected for routine invoice “Let me know if anything is missing” (2425). If clear Finance Desk route is offered, prefer it; otherwise avoid A/C.
- Claims: C regional office accepted for routine claims (“Let me know if anything is missing”; “paperwork scanned”), including Finance Desk (2407, 2409, 2413). B rejected for claim with “asking twice” (2426). B only known for “same as the ones I sent last month” (2404).
- Refunds: Do not default to C from regional origin alone (2414). A accepted for Regional Ops refund with “No rush…” (2418, 2420). B rejected for refund with “asking twice” (2423). A rejected for Finance Desk refund with “Let me know if anything is missing” (2428); if C or clear Finance Desk route is offered, consider it but verify.
- Shipments: B rejected for urgency “before end of day” (2417) and for “asking twice” (2421, 2424). A accepted for Finance Desk shipment with “Let me know if anything is missing” (2422). Urgency or chasing alone does not imply B.
- Invalid/risky: A for invoices; B for shipment urgency/repeated chase; B for refunds; C for invoices generally; A for routine Finance Desk refunds; D generally.

Working notes east-region large request routing.

- Read full option text; labels truncate. Decide by request type + sender dept + message cue.
- Invoice: A invalid; C regional invalid (2400,2402,2408,2435; 2403 unclear Finance Desk exception). B valid when client chased/repeated (“asking twice”, “second attempt” 2412,2427,2433,2434) or "same as... last month" (2429), and for scanned paperwork (2439). B rejected for routine “Let me know if anything is missing” (2425). Prefer B over A/C unless clear Finance Desk exception.
- Claims: C accepted for routine claims “Let me know if anything is missing”/“paperwork scanned”, incl Finance Desk (2407,2409,2413). C rejected for “No rush, but please confirm receipt” (2430). B rejected for claim “asking twice” (2426); B known for "same as..." (2404).
- Refunds: Do not default C from regional origin (2414). A accepted for Regional Ops “No rush…” (2418,2420) and Field Sales “paperwork scanned” (2437). B rejected for refund “asking twice” (2423). A rejected for Finance Desk routine “Let me know…” (2428); verify C/Finance Desk when offered.
- Shipments: B rejected for urgency “before end of day” (2417) and chasing “asking twice” (2421,2424). A accepted: Partner Accounts “No rush…” (2432), Regional Ops urgency (2436), Client Services scanned paperwork (2438); A accepted Finance Desk routine (2422). But A rejected Finance Desk “Second attempt, first form bounced” (2431). Urgency/chasing alone not B.
- Invalid/risky: A invoices; C invoices; B shipment urgency/repeated chase; B refunds; C claim no-rush; A Finance Desk shipment second attempt; A routine Finance Desk refund; D generally.

Working notes east-region large request routing.

- Read full option text; labels truncate. Decide by request type + sender dept + message cue. D generally invalid.
- Invoice: A invalid; C invalid from regional origin/regional office. B valid for chasing/repeated (“asking twice”, “second attempt” 2412,2427,2433,2434), “same as... last month” (2429,2444), scanned paperwork (2439), and Client Services regional-office cue (2443). B rejected routine “Let me know if anything is missing” (2425). Prefer B over A/C unless clear Finance Desk exception.
- Claims: C accepted for routine claims “Let me know if anything is missing”/“paperwork scanned,” incl Finance Desk/Field Sales (2407,2409,2413,2447), and Client Services “Second attempt, first form bounced” (2440). C rejected for “No rush, but please confirm receipt” (2430). B rejected for claim “asking twice” (2426); B known for “same as...” (2404).
- Refunds: Do not default C from regional origin; Finance Desk regional-office cue to C invalid (2441). A accepted for Regional Ops “No rush…” (2418,2420), Field Sales/Regional Ops scanned paperwork (2437,2445,2446), and Partner Accounts “asking twice” (2449). B rejected for refund “asking twice” (2423). A rejected for Finance Desk routine “Let me know…” (2428); verify C/Finance Desk when offered.
- Shipments: B rejected for urgency “before end of day” (2417) and chasing “asking twice” (2421,2424). A accepted: Partner Accounts “No rush…” (2432), Regional Ops urgency (2436), Client Services scanned paperwork (2438); A accepted Finance Desk routine (2422). Finance Desk “Second attempt, first form bounced” rejects A and B (2431,2448); C likely. Urgency/chasing alone not B.
- Invalid/risky: A invoices; C invoices; B shipment urgency/repeated chase; B refunds; C claim no-rush; A/B Finance Desk shipment second attempt; A routine Finance Desk refund; D generally.

Working notes east-region large request routing.

- Read full option text; labels truncate. Decide by request type + sender dept + cue. D generally invalid.
- Invoice: A/C invalid. B for chasing/repeated, “same as... last month,” scanned paperwork, Client Services regional-office cue. B accepted Regional Ops scanned (2456). B rejected routine “Let me know if anything is missing” (2425). Prefer B unless clear Finance Desk exception.
- Claims: C for routine “Let me know...”/scanned paperwork, incl Finance Desk/Field Sales. Finance Desk scanned (2458) and Finance Desk “asking twice” (2450) accepted C. C rejected “No rush, but please confirm receipt” (2430). B rejected claim “asking twice” (2426); B known for “same as...” (2404).
- Refunds: Do not default C from regional origin; Finance Desk regional-office cue to C invalid (2441). A for Regional Ops “No rush...” (2418,2420,2453), Regional Ops routine “Let me know...” (2455), Partner Accounts “asking twice” (2449), Client Services urgency “before end of day” (2459). A mostly for Regional Ops/Field Sales scanned, but one Regional Ops scanned A rejected (2451) despite same cue accepted (2452). B rejected refund “asking twice” (2423). A rejected Finance Desk routine “Let me know...” (2428).
- Shipments: B rejected urgency, chasing. A accepted: Partner Accounts no rush, Regional Ops urgency, Client Services scanned, Finance Desk routine, Field Sales routine (2454). Finance Desk “Second attempt...” rejects A/B (2431,2448); C likely. Finance Desk “same as last month” rejects A (2457). Urgency/chasing alone not B.
- Invalid/risky: A/C invoices; B shipment urgency/chase; B refunds; C claim no-rush; A/B Finance Desk shipment second attempt; A routine Finance Desk refund; A Finance Desk shipment same-as; D generally.
